configs.description: The unit with one power supply kit fitted, as the rear photograph shows it. The page lists the kit as a mandatory accessory and the photograph does not say which of the two it is.
configs.name: default

gaps.note: The held photographs show the front and the rear only. The four other faces are sized from the product page and drawn empty.
gaps.wanted: A photograph or drawing of the sides, the top and the underside.

gaps.note: The rear photograph shows the two WWAN openings as plain dark circles with no connector visible at 8 times. This file draws gold SMA jacks there. The jacks are kept, because the maker lists SMA on the CORE plug-in modem of the Connect EZ 16/32. The SD slot is the library's full-size SD slot, sized from another maker's photograph (the page lists "(1) SD/SDHC/SDXC socket" and no size). The system fan is drawn as a honeycomb grille and a thumbscrew, not as a replaceable part, because no held document says it is one. Its openings are fainter than the photograph's bright ones. The photograph also shows four small case screws at the fan module's corners, which are not drawn. The right-hand power supply's second thumbscrew and the PSU1 and PSU2 legends on the supplies' outer tabs are not drawn. The cover plate's small screws are not all drawn.
gaps.wanted: Digi's hardware guide, or a close photograph of the rear.

gaps.note: The page makes one of two kits mandatory, ITPS-PSEK (port-side exhaust) or ITPS-PSIK (port-side intake), and the rear photograph does not say which it shows. Both bays seat one supply part that states neither kit and no airflow.
gaps.wanted: A photograph of each kit, or the hardware guide's description of the two.

gaps.note: The round button under the power and status lamps carries a symbol that does not resolve at 800 px and no document names its function, so it is drawn as a plain button and not as a part. The marks under the Ethernet, SFP+ and USB housings (a number and an arrow each) do not resolve and are not drawn. The bright metal frame that joins the serial jacks of each block is drawn as one solid plate per block, 116 x 30.4. The photograph shows a thin outline and a bar between the rows, so each plate stands for both. It is read off the front photograph at 4 times with 1.53 px/mm across. Its colour is the mean of 509 bright bar pixels. The bright frame round the console jack and the USB ports, and the outline of the SFP+ cage, are not drawn.
gaps.wanted: Digi's hardware guide, or a higher resolution photograph of the front.

gaps.note: The photographs are 800 px wide. The legends that resolve are drawn; the rating text beside the power supply inlets is drawn as it reads, and the small marks that do not resolve are not.
gaps.wanted: A higher resolution photograph of each face.

gaps.note: The page names the lamps and no colour or state of any of them.
The page lists no rail or mounting kit for the unit and no document held describes the rack ears.
The page gives one consumption figure for the unit and none for a supply, the fan or the CORE modem, so no module states one.

gaps.wanted: an `attrs.performance` section; `attrs.platform.cpu`; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in `attrs.environmental` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 2 bays (rear 2) - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: The product page prints "444 mm x 300 mm x 44 mm (17.48 in x 11.81 in x 1.73 in)" labelled L x W x H, one row for both sizes. Read with the photographs and the 1U height, 444 is the width of the body between the ear folds, 300 the depth and 44 the height. The label's order does not say so, and no drawing confirms it.

colour.note: The front and rear are black, the jacks have bright metal shields, the USB tongues are blue, the rack ears are black and the thumbscrews have a blue ring.

ears.note: The front photograph shows a rack ear on each side, flush with the face and holding two slotted holes. The page says nothing of ears or a rail kit. No position other than the one photographed is stated, and no distance behind the face is measured.

front-layout.note: From the front photograph: two Ethernet jacks stacked at 24.1, two SFP+ cages stacked at 43.0, the console jack and two USB Type A ports in one housing centred at 69.4, and forty-eight serial jacks in two rows, the odd numbers below, in three blocks of eight columns from 83.85 on a 14.2 pitch with 5.9 between the blocks (the blocks start 119.5 apart). The pitch was read off the numerals of the 16-port front, which has the same layout, and sits 1.6 per cent above the registry's 13.97. The last numeral stands 2 mm short of where this photograph puts it. The row of round vents along the top runs from 82 to 429 on a 4.15 pitch. The power and status lamps are at 19.0, 18.5 and 24.3 down; the round button below them is at 10.5, 34.3 down.

gate-1.note: The front photograph spans 678 px for the 444 mm body between the ears (1.53 px/mm) and the rear 731 px for the 444 mm body (1.65 px/mm). The photographs include the top edge of the box, so across is read at the scale above and down is a fraction of the face's own height (44 mm) read off its top and bottom edges. Every position is good to about 2 mm.

lamps.note: The page lists "Front: device power, status; (2) Ethernet (link/active) console (Tx/Rx); 16/48 (Tx/Rx); Back: (2) PSU, status, WWAN signal/service". The rear photograph prints WWAN Signal, WWAN Service, PSU1, PSU2 and Status. Nothing states a colour or a state, so the system lamps carry on and off only.

ports.note: The product page lists "(48) RS-232 serial RJ-45 (support standard or reversed mode)", "(1) RS-232 serial RJ-45 console port", "(2) 10/100/1000 Ethernet", "(2) 10 Gb capable SFP+ sockets", "(2) USB 3.1 Gen 1 (Type A)" and an SD socket. The standard or reversed setting is a pinout setting and is not drawn.

power.note: "Redundant 100-240 V ~ 50-60 Hz 2.4 A max for each power supply" and "POWER CONSUMPTION 39 W" for this size. The page does not say whether the figure is typical or maximum, so it is filed as the maximum. The mandatory kit supplies the two replaceable supplies.

rear-layout.note: From the rear photograph, which both sizes share: the power supply bays are 94 wide at each end, the CORE plate 96 to 301, the system fan grille 40 across centred at 322.5, the SD slot and reset pinhole on a cover plate at 233.6, and five lamps at 295.5 from 13.3 down on a 5.2 pitch. The two WWAN openings are centred at 116.3 and 208.0, 31.4 down, about 7 mm across.

sources.note: Digi Connect IT 16/48 product page (digi.com, read 2026-11-05): ports, lamps, power, size, weight and part numbers. The Connect IT 48 front photograph and the shared rear photograph (800 px wide each, straight on): every position, legend and colour below. No data sheet or user guide is held; the data sheet is behind a form on the maker's site and the user guide is a link to a document not held. No dimension model is held.

weight.note: "5.28 kg (11.65 lbs) with power supply kit installed" for this size.
